Both versions use 64-bit unsigned integers. Past N=91 they overflow and wrap around instead of printing the true value. For larger N you'd need `u128` in Rust and a custom print routine in C++.

**How it works:** the first line is `//\`. C++ treats the backslash as a line continuation, so the next line (`/*`) is part of the comment.
